core: reading normal output and traceback output

claims.claim: Starting Python without a script enters interactive mode when its standard input is a terminal, where primary prompts accept commands and display results of expressions.
Giving Python a script file causes the interpreter to read and execute that file.
The -c option runs the command supplied as a string.
When a module is run as the top-level program, its __name__ is set to '__main__'.
A traceback reports the call stack at an exception; the final line identifies the exception type and its detail.
In a script, statements run in order until execution ends or an unhandled exception interrupts it.
